messages:
incident-bot: PAGER ALERT: High-severity security incident detected: multiple failed auth attempts followed by successful token usage from a rare geo (CN). Automated detector also flagged a public S3 object that appears to contain redacted logs but contains partial auth tokens. Merged incident ticket: INC-4382. Please ack.

Maria Lopez: Acked. I'm on-call. looking now. Can someone drop the IP list?

Tom Nguyen: Adding the IPs to the WAF blocklist now. IPs: 45.77.33.12, 104.131.44.55, 203.0.113.7

Tom Nguyen: (command)
```
aws wafv2 update-ip-set --name suspicious-ips --addresses 45.77.33.12/32 104.131.44.55/32 203.0.113.7/32 --scope REGIONAL
```

Maria Lopez: Confirmed blocked at edge. Next: are we sure tokens leaked? any env/API keys in those S3 objects?

Ajay Patel: I grabbed a sample object from the bucket (public-read). It looks like rotated-out request logs but a few lines with Authorization: Bearer <redacted> where the token suffix is present. I'm pulling the full grep now. Snippet:
```
GET /v1/generate 200
Authorization: Bearer sk-prod-abc123...def456
```

Ajay Patel: We should assume tokens were compromised. Immediate actions: 1) Revoke any active prod API keys older than 48h, 2) rotate the one identified, 3) force reissue of any session tokens for affected services.

Emily Carter: Notifying impacted customers: I have a template but need list of customers who had requests tied to the leaked tokens. Can engineering produce list of customer_ids that used those tokens?

Maria Lopez: Running a query on request logs to match token suffix 'def456' across regions. Query takes ~2m.

DevOps Bot: Query job started: job_id=ql-7823. Estimated 120s. Link: https://analytics.prod/jobs/ql-7823

Tom Nguyen: Also found elevated egress to strange IPs from inference-gpu-prod-2 between 02:15-02:27 UTC. Capturing pcap and netflow. Dumping suspected connections to S3 for forensics. Command:
```
sudo tcpdump -w /tmp/egress-suspect.pcap host 45.77.33.12
aws s3 cp /tmp/egress-suspect.pcap s3://sec-artifacts/INC-4382/
```

Maria Lopez: Result from log query: matched 6 customer_ids: cust_92, cust_114, cust_201, cust_312, cust_401, cust_512. Sharing to Emily.

Emily Carter: Thanks. I'll start tailored notifications using the security template. tagging legal and account teams. cc @Kelly Rivera.

Kelly Rivera: On it. Will coordinate with legal and prepare SLA impact notes. Also need timeline for when key rotation completes so we can include remediation steps for customers.

Ajay Patel: I'm rotating the exposed API key now. Steps: revoke via admin console, create new key, update service account and CI secrets. Will push a canary rotation to non-critical pool first.

Ajay Patel: Commands:
```
# revoke
curl -X POST https://admin.prod/api/keys/revoke -H 'Authorization: Bearer ADMIN_TOKEN' -d '{"key_id":"sk-prod-abc123"}'
# create
curl -X POST https://admin.prod/api/keys/create -H 'Authorization: Bearer ADMIN_TOKEN' -d '{"name":"rotated-INC-4382"}'
```

Ajay Patel: Revoke done. New key created: sk-prod-rot-9f4d. Updating Vault.

DevOps Bot: Vault update job enqueued: job_id=vlt-5591. Status: pending.

Ajay Patel: Vault update completed. CI secrets updated in staging, starting canary deploy to 3 instances.

Tom Nguyen: Canary looks stable. No auth errors. Rolling to remaining pool. Blocking old key at edge (WAF + token blacklist).

Maria Lopez: Handoff note: I need to go offline for scheduled handover in 18m. @Ajay Patel will be primary oncall. Ajay, confirm you have runbook link and custody of evidence.

Ajay Patel: Confirmed. Runbook: https://confluence.redwood/runbooks/sec-key-leak. Evidence in s3://sec-artifacts/INC-4382/. I've also handed off pcap to forensics.

Compliance Bot: Notifying SOC and recording incident for PCI/ISO tracking. Ticket INC-4382 updated. Retention policy applied to artifacts bucket.

Kelly Rivera: Quick question — are any customer plaintext logs exposed? we need to widen notification if so.

Ajay Patel: Initial inspection: logs included request headers and some obfuscated payloads. No direct PII detected in the sampled objects, but we'll do a full grep for email, ssn, etc. For now treat as potential exposure.

Emily Carter: Legal says send preliminary notice with "no evidence of customer PII at this time" but we must be transparent about token exposure and actions taken.

Maria Lopez: During handoff: I confirmed WAF blocks, key revoked, rotation complete, Vault updated, forensics pcap uploaded, customers identified. Leaving notes in INC-4382. Back afterwards if needed.

Ajay Patel: Continuing monitoring: setting higher alert thresholds and adding temporary rule to drop egress to known malicious CIDRs. Also enabling stricter token expiry policy for next 24h.

DevOps Bot: Egress block applied: cidr-set-24 updated. Job id netblk-221.

Tom Nguyen: Confirmed no further suspicious auths in last 30m. Rate of failed auth spikes back to baseline.

Emily Carter: Customer notifications dispatched (initial) to affected list. Shared copies with legal and accounts. Template: https://confluence.redwood/templates/sec-notify.

Kelly Rivera: Good. Let's schedule an incident review tomorrow 10:00 UTC. Postmortem owner: Maria Lopez. Severity: P1 -> Security. Follow-up actions: rotate any long-lived keys, S3 audit for public ACLs, tighter CI secret rotates, update runbooks.

Ajay Patel: Also recommending immediate org-wide forced rotation for any keys older than 90 days. Raise as action item.

Maria Lopez: Handoff complete. Ajay taking over. If anything pops I'll rejoin. :hand:

Ajay Patel: Acknowledged. Logging final mitigation summary in incident ticket and will coordinate postmortem.

incident-bot: INCIDENT UPDATE: INC-4382 mitigations recorded. Status: mitigated -> monitoring. Postmortem scheduled. Links: https://incidents.redwood/INC-4382
